back: A business owned by two or more people who carry it on together to make a profit, sharing profits, risks and decisions.
The partners' agreement (preferably written) on capital, profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital and drawings, salaries, loans and duties.
Partners are personally responsible for all the business's debts; their private possessions can be used to pay them.

front: Profit sharing when there is no partnership agreement
back: Shared equally; no interest on capital, no salaries, no interest on drawings; interest on partners' loans at 5% a year.

front: Where does interest on a partner's loan go?
back: Income statement, as an expense (before profit for the year). It is NOT an appropriation.
To reward the partner who has invested more money (and taken more risk) before the rest is shared.
To discourage partners from taking money out early or in large amounts.

front: Entry when a partner brings an asset into the business
back: Debit the asset account; credit that partner's capital account.
Unlimited liability; profits shared; disagreements; less capital than a company; ends on a partner's death or departure.
